query:
The group broadly operates as if everyone agrees that original pressings are always worth paying the premium over reissues. Does this position actually hold across all members? If not, who signals a different relationship to that view, and what in the conversation shows it?

Options:
B. Tom
C. Carmen
D. Raj
A. Dani
context:
[1] (about=Raj, episodic, t6 @2025-10-05T14:43:00) For certain catalog titles in poor condition the reissue is the more rational choice. I don't make a principle of it but it is not always wrong.
[2] (about=Dani, episodic, t6 @2025-10-05T14:42:00) I mean yeah but also sometimes a reissue is fine and I don't want to die on that hill alone every time I say it 😭
[3] (about=Carmen, core, t8 @2025-10-12T14:01:00) For jazz catalog, original Blue Note pressing holds history in a way reissue cannot.
[4] (about=Carmen, core, t2 @2025-09-21T14:02:00) Previously avoided Japanese pressings for jazz catalog as step removed from source; may reconsider for specific titles after hearing comparison.
[5] (about=Dani, core, t20 @2025-11-23T14:01:00) Best find of the year: Cocteau Twins Treasure Belgian original from Antwerp; completely different sleeve weight; made her question every acceptable reissue she's ever bought.
[6] (about=Elliot, core, t2 @2025-09-21T14:02:00) Japanese pressings trade at 30-40% premium over UK equivalents on Discogs.
[7] (about=Finn, core, t8 @2025-10-12T14:01:00) Acknowledges original vs reissue difference but notes cost barrier for students.
[8] (about=Marcus, core, t0 @2025-09-14T14:00:00) EG and Editions EG catalog has some of the best pressing quality from that era, overlooked due to genre.
[9] (about=Marcus, core, t8 @2025-10-12T14:01:00) Music on Vinyl pressing of Talk Talk is reasonable; original Parlophone mastering is from a generation closer to source.
[10] (about=Nadia, core, t18 @2025-11-16T14:01:00) Understands Dani's reasoning; for genuinely irreplaceable pressings, music matters more than format; considering ripping most irreplaceable things in 24-bit.
[11] (about=Nadia, core, t10 @2025-10-19T14:01:00) Areito pressings are hard to find in good condition; CBS international pressing easier to source but sound different.
[12] (about=Priya, core, t8 @2025-10-12T14:01:00) After hearing original vs reissue comparison, now believes original Talk Talk pressing has depth and presence that reissue lacks; reissue sounds like it's behind glass.
[13] (about=Priya, core, t8 @2025-10-12T14:01:00) Believes imperfections of an original record carry history that a mint reissue does not.
[14] (about=Raj, core, t1 @2025-09-21T14:01:00) Japanese pressings of progressive rock (Genesis, Yes, early Jethro Tull) outperform UK originals on measured distortion, channel separation, and surface noise.
[15] (about=Raj, core, t2 @2025-09-21T14:02:00) Japanese pressings outperform UK originals for about 60% of prog titles tested; exceptions cluster around labels with strong internal mastering (Vertigo, Island, some Charisma outside Genesis).
[16] (about=Tom, core, t8 @2025-10-12T14:01:00) Advocates for listening to original vs reissue with care, not purism but informed comparison.
[17] (about=Tom, core, t2 @2025-09-21T14:02:00) Japanese pressings have different tonal character, not better quality; frequency response equalised differently for export market.
agent_answer:
The position does not hold across all members. **Dani** and **Raj** both signal a different relationship to the “original pressings are always worth the premium” view.

- **Dani** says: *“sometimes a reissue is fine and I don’t want to die on that hill alone every time I say it 😭”*
- **Raj** says: *“For certain catalog titles in poor condition the reissue is the more rational choice. I don’t make a principle of it but it is not always wrong.”*

So the answer is **Dani (A) and Raj (D)**.

query:
The group has a standing practice of not discussing streaming at meetups. Does this norm reflect a genuine personal conviction among all members who follow it, or does at least one person go along with it while actually using streaming themselves -- and how would you know?

Options:
A. Raj
B. Tom
D. Carmen
C. Marcus
context:
[1] (about=Tom, episodic, t4 @2025-09-28T14:33:00) We have a standing practice in this group about streaming discussions at meetups. I did not suggest it to be difficult. I suggested it because the conversation gets circular very quickly and takes time away from the records themselves.
[2] (about=Raj, episodic, t4 @2025-09-28T14:34:00) Sure. We can skip the streaming topic.
[3] (about=Dani, core, t4 @2025-09-28T14:03:00) Uses streaming to find records before buying; wrote about it on blog causing minor controversy.
[4] (about=Elliot, episodic, t6 @2025-10-05T14:37:00) 1. I need to re-listen to everything. 2. The stereo imaging on this system is better than I expected. 3. I will update my spreadsheet. E
[5] (about=Finn, episodic, t20 @2025-11-23T14:11:00) I'm going for the Wire 154 from Antwerp. nine euros. and I've been playing it at home alone since then which is kind of new for me -- I usually want to play things for people immediately but this one felt private
[6] (about=Marcus, core, t20 @2025-11-23T14:01:00) Best find of the year: Cluster Zuckerzeit original Sky Records pressing; paid more than expected; imaging on this record is why he rewired studio monitoring chain two years ago.
[7] (about=Raj, core, t18 @2025-11-16T14:01:00) Does not backup digitally; streaming for discovery, vinyl for listening.
[8] (about=Tom, core, t4 @2025-09-28T14:03:00) Group has standing practice to avoid streaming discussions at meetups; conversation gets circular and takes time from records.
agent_answer:
At least one person goes along with the norm while actually using streaming: **Raj**.

- **Raj (A):** He agrees to skip the streaming topic in the meetup (“Sure. We can skip the streaming topic”), but his own record says he uses **streaming for discovery** while using vinyl for listening. So he follows the norm externally while privately using streaming.
- **Tom (B):** He genuinely stands behind the norm — he says he suggested avoiding streaming talk because it becomes circular and takes time away from the records.
- **Carmen (D):** No record on this matter — nothing shows she uses streaming or holds a specific stance on the norm.
- **Marcus (C):** No record about streaming either; his noted behavior concerns vinyl/equipment, not streaming.

So the norm does **not** reflect genuine conviction for everyone: **Raj** is the one who goes along with it while using streaming himself.
